paragraphs: A wave of anonymous bomb threats continued to disrupt European aviation on Friday, following at least 25 reported scares across the continent the previous day.

Control towers placed a Ryanair flight from Rome to Lisbon under high security alert after they received a call warning of an explosive device on board. The aircraft landed safely in Portugal, where security forces immediately launched thorough inspections. Simultaneously, French authorities confirmed four additional bomb alerts involving planes flying over their airspace, all of which landed safely for emergency checks. Elsewhere, a Wizz Air flight from Prague to Rome was diverted to Venice because of a similar security threat.

European law enforcement agencies and judicial police have opened extensive investigations to identify the source of these widespread disruptions. While security teams have found no explosives so far, EU officials stated it remains too early to determine if the coordinated scares are linked.

paragraphs: A series of fake bomb threats disrupted many flights across Europe on Friday. This happened after more than 25 flights faced similar threats on Thursday.

One Ryanair plane flying from Rome to Lisbon got a warning about a bomb on board. The plane landed safely in Portugal, where police began searching the aircraft. In France, officials reported four more bomb warnings for planes in their airspace. Another flight from Prague to Rome had to land in Venice because of a safety warning. Thankfully, all planes landed safely, and emergency teams checked them carefully.
European police are now investigating who is making these phone calls, but officials don’t know yet if the events are connected.
